subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Shifting Reference Points in Pricing
description: A quick, practical guide to Shifting Reference Points in Pricing.

hook.text: A shirt marked down from $80 to $40 feels like a deal. The same shirt always priced at $40 feels average.

buildup.text: Retailers use the original price as a reference anchor. The discount is measured against what you 'saved.'

discovery.text: The anchor price sets your reference. Every cent below it feels like a gain, making the purchase feel smart.

twist.text: Some retailers inflate original prices specifically to create a larger perceived discount. The anchor was a fiction.

climax.text: Ignore the original price. Ask: is this item worth this amount to me right now? That's the real question.

punchline.text: A deal isn't a deal if you didn't need it.

quiz.question: Why do strikethrough prices make discounts feel bigger?
options: The original price sets a high reference point
All discounted items are better quality

details.summary: Businesses strategically manipulate reference points to make prices feel like bargains. Showing a high original price, listing a premium option first, or anchoring with a competitor's higher price shifts the reference point to make the actual price feel like a gain.
details.whyItMatters: Every pricing strategy is ultimately a reference point strategy. Understanding how businesses set and shift reference points reveals the psychology behind why the same price can feel cheap or expensive depending on context.
takeaways: Anchor prices set high reference points that make real prices feel like gains
Decoy options shift reference points to favor the target product
Context and comparison determine perceived value more than actual price

faq.question: How does the decoy effect work in pricing?
faq.answer: A third option is added that is clearly worse than one choice but comparable to another, making the favored option look better by comparison. A medium coffee priced near the large makes the large seem like better value, shifting your reference.

faq.question: Why do luxury brands never discount products?
faq.answer: Discounting reveals a lower reference point and makes the full price feel like a loss. By never discounting, luxury brands maintain a stable reference point where the high price is perceived as fair value rather than an overcharge.
